name: Arzl im Pitztal
kurzbeschreibung: Innsbruck is the main town of the Pitztal, offering direct access to the glacier ski area and the breathtaking Pitztaler Höhenweg.
beschreibung:
Overview

Arzl im Pitztal is located at an elevation of 880 meters on a sunny plateau at the entrance of the Pitztal valley in Tyrol's Imst district, situated high above the Inn Valley and the rugged Arzler Pitzeklamm gorge. Framed by Mount Tschirgant to the north, Mount Venet to the southwest, and the Leiner Kögele to the northeast, the village proudly serves as the 'Gateway to the Pitztal'. With roughly 3,200 residents, Arzl is the most populous municipality and principal hub of the valley. Encompassing the main village alongside the picturesque hamlets of Wald, Leins, Timls, Hochasten, Blons, and Osterstein, Arzl combines deep agricultural traditions with outstanding access to high-alpine glaciers and trails.

History

The village name derives from the Rhaeto-Romanic word arcella, meaning 'little castle', referencing a prehistoric fortified hill on the 'Burgstall' mound—a heritage reflected in the battlemented silver chevron on the municipal coat of arms. The settlements of Wald and Hochasten were recorded around 1070 in records of the Bishopric of Brixen, while Arzl itself was first documented in 1260 when nobleman Gebhart von Starkenberg deeded tithes to Wilten Abbey. Historically renowned for fruit orchards and premium Tyrolean mountain potatoes, Arzl is also the proud hometown of double Olympic alpine skiing champion Benjamin Raich and rock band Mother's Cake.

Getting There

Access to Arzl is remarkably straightforward: motorists take the Inntal Motorway A12 to exit 133 Imst/Pitztal and follow the Pitztaler Landesstraße L16 for just four kilometers into the village center (approximately five minutes). From southern Germany, drivers can arrive toll-free across the Fern Pass highway B179 via Reutte. By rail, Imst-Pitztal railway station on the Arlberg main line accommodates Railjet and regional trains from Innsbruck, Zurich, and Vienna. VVT regional bus line 4204 operates frequent shuttles from the station to Arzl in five to eight minutes, free of charge for guests holding the Pitztal Leisure Card.

Tips

The undisputed highlight is the Benni Raich Bridge across the Pitzeklamm gorge: suspended 94 meters above the canyon with a 138-meter span, it ranks among Europe's highest pedestrian suspension bridges and hosts international bungee jumping. Nearby, the dramatic Adlerhorst cantilevered viewing platform provides sweeping views over the Inn Valley and Kaunergrat Nature Park, reachable also via the athletic Steinwand Via Ferrata (grade C/D). Visitors should also see the Gothic-Baroque Parish Church of Saints Ingenuin and Albuin, featuring a covered wooden bridge connecting to the rectory. The town is the classic base for the Pitztal High Trail and high-altitude trips to the Pitztal Glacier with its Cafe 3,440. Local culinary delights center on famed Arzl potato dishes.
